title: Token diagnostics playbook — wireframes & notes
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a Token Diagnostics view in the Console. Goal is to give engineers and product owners a compact, action-oriented UX for per-token cost + latency attribution with fast triage flows (investigate slow tokens, regressions, cold-starts, private deployments). This doc mixes wireframe notes, interaction patterns, data sampling strategies, and a prioritized backlog for an initial MVP + two followups.

High-level user needs (ranked):
1) Root cause: "Why did this request cost X and take Y ms?" (team: infra, SRE, eng owners)
2) Quick correlation: token positions vs. model variants / quantization / batching / region (ML infra + infraops)
3) Lightweight drilldown: jump from a token to the sample prompt + config + blob of KV cache hits/misses
4) Shareable snapshot: generate a short permalink for ticket handoff (security: redaction options)
5) Mobile microview: support on-call glance for incidents (push-optimized)

Personas:
- Platform SRE (Latency-focused) — needs percentile view and tail diagnostics.
- Model Ops / Applied ML (Quality + Cost) — needs per-token cost and embeddings impact.
- Developer (Feature owner) — wants fast link to request examples and rollout info.
- Support / CS — needs redacted shareable snapshots and simple explainers.

MVP scope (horizontal):
- Per-request list w/ token-level breakdown heatmap (tokens as columns, time progression as rows)
- Token metrics: token-index, token-text (optional), token-latency-ms, token-cost-cents, cache-hit (bool), kv-size, device (GPU/CPU), model-variant tag
- Request metadata: request-id, model-name+version, region, route, user-team, start_ts, latency_ms_total, tokens_input, tokens_output, batching-group (id)
- Drill-in panel: shows original request, config (temperature, max_tokens, quantize profile), and a per-token timeline with hover details
- Snapshot export: JSON export for engineers; redacted export option to mask prompt text

Wireframe notes (desktop):
- Main panel: Request stream on left (compact list). Center: selected request canvas with token heatmap. Right: timeline + config + quick-actions.
- Heatmap: color scale for latency per token (green=fast, red=slow). Secondary overlay: pale outline for cost per-token to indicate expensive tokens even if low latency (e.g., billing weight).
- Hover card: shows token-text (if permitted), latency-ms, cost-cents, cache-hit, KV hit reason (prefix match / exact), and link to related batch events.
- Timeline scrubber: play through token generation with animated marker to reproduce timing. Playback speed options 0.5x/1x/2x and 'step to tail ms'.
- Actions above canvas: [Create Incident] [Export snapshot] [Open in Profiler] [Compare variant]. Compare variant opens a split view with same request executed on selected variants.

Mobile microview ideas (on-call):
- Single-column: top shows summary (latency, cost, error rate). Below: most-suspicious-token (index+reason) with one-tap copy to clipboard and create-incident.
- Use compact sparklines (1-line) rather than full heatmap.
- Fallback: if prompt is redacted for SHARED_USERS, show redaction badge and provide admin-only expand.

Privacy & redaction rules:
- Default public snapshots must strip prompt / token-text. Admins can enable "show tokens" via role-based flag.
- EU customers: by default do not allow raw prompt export for Private deployments without KMS tag.
- Store token-text only for 30 days in the analysis index; store aggregated metrics longer.

Sampling and telemetry strategy (practical constraints):
- Full token capture for all requests is expensive. Sampling tiers:
  - Tier A (100%): reserved for Dedicated customers + flagged incidents
  - Tier B (10%): random sampling across hosted API for derived metrics
  - Tier C (0.1%): for raw-token retention for top 1% high-cost requests
- Heuristics to mark requests for full capture: tail latency > 99th percentile, cost per request > 95th percentile, or explicit customer flag via API header (X-RI-debug).
- Batching correlation: log batch id, position within batch, and per-batch throughput so we can attribute per-token extra wait time due to batching window.

Data schema (flattened list for analytics index - keep small):
- request_id, tenant_id, model, model_variant, region, route, start_ts, end_ts, total_latency_ms, total_cost_cents, tokens_in, tokens_out, batch_id, batch_size, hardware_type, quant_profile, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, sample_flag
- token_index_N, token_text_N (optional/privileged), token_latency_ms_N, token_cost_cents_N, device_N, kv_hit_N
(note: implementation reality — token_N fields are stored in a separate row per token in the analysis table; keeping request-level index simplifies product UX)

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console shows list of requests filtered by route + last 24h with sortable latency and cost columns.
- Clicking request opens token heatmap; hover shows per-token details.
- Export snapshot produces a JSON with metadata and either redacted OR full tokens per RBAC.
- Query performance: open drill panel for a request in <1.2s for recent (24h) events.

Backlog (prioritized rough estimates):
- P0: Token heatmap + hover details + export snapshot (3 sprints)
- P1: Compare variant split view + timeline playback (2 sprints)
- P1: Mobile microview (1 sprint)
- P2: Smart suggestions (root cause hints: e.g., heavy KV miss, batching wait) (2 sprints)
- P2: Integration w/ profiler (profiler opens selected token timestamp) (2 sprints)
- P3: Per-tenant retention config UI + compliance toggles (1 sprint)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we show full token text in UI by default for internal users? (security vs. speed of debugging.)
- Sampling: should we bias towards error responses or natural tail? Proposed: hybrid (tail+random).
- How to surface batching-induced latency vs. model compute latency? Need a standard annotation from serving runtime (batch_wait_ms vs compute_ms).
- Should the export snapshot include a tiny cost-explain (per-token billing determinant) string? (Yes if not leaking alt-sensitive info).

Design constraints and implementation notes for eng teams:
- Backend: token-level events must be indexed with request_id and time offset in ms. Use dedicated index with TTL to avoid cost explosion.
- UI: render large requests lazily; only render visible token window; compressed rendering for >2k tokens (scroll + aggregate blocks).
- Perf: server should precompute heatmap buckets per request at ingestion time for faster UX.
- Auth: snapshot perm checks should be evaluated server-side before export generation.

Example flow (incident triage):
1) Pager triggers: alert shows increased 99.9th latency for route /chat/completion.
2) On-call opens Token Diagnostics, filters to route and last 15 minutes, sorts by total latency.
3) Select top request, open heatmap; identify token 128 with 400ms latency and KV miss.
4) Click token -> shows KV key, last update time, originating model variant; create incident with prefilled snapshot and link to GitHub PR that rolled out variant.

Sketch of a short copy for empty-state and hover microcopy (for designers):
- Empty state: "No token captures found. Try widening the time range or enable full capture for this tenant."
- Hover microcopy for a token latency: "Token latency: compute (xx ms) + queue (yy ms). Click to see batch profile."

Accessibility and localization notes:
- Heatmap should have high-contrast palette for colorblind+low-vision. Add numeric overlay toggle.
- Microcopy must be localizable; try to keep hover strings short (<90 chars).

Next steps (immediate):
- Product to align with Applied ML on the metrics fields we must capture. (Owner: Maya) — due EOD next Tue.
- Engineering spike to estimate storage + index costs for 30d retention of token metrics (Owner: Arjun) — 1 week.
- Design to produce two desktop wireframes and a single mobile microview by next design review. (Owner: Samira) — 8 business days.

Notes-to-self / rough items to add later:
- Quick A/B UX test script for whether showing full token text accelerates triage time (two cohorts).
- Placeholder images: mockup-1.png (heatmap), mockup-2.png (mobile microview) — designers will add to Drive.

Recent related links / references (internal):
- perf-playbook: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/ops/playbooks#token-latency
- profile-integration RFC: CONFLUENCE-9876

End of doc (working).
